intro: Lesson 29. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: أَلْهَىٰكُمُ ٱلتَّكَاثُرُ (١) حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ (٢) كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (٣) ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: No! You are going to know.
Then no! You are going to know.

questions.q: Chunk and link At-Takathur 102:1-4 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 102:1-4 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Tell a grown-up three things you are thankful for.

questions.a: A) distracts us. 102:1: 'Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you.'

questions.q: Think again: Some people always want more toys, more money, more things. Can 'more' ever be enough?
questions.a: Wanting more and more distracts us from Allah (102:1). We are thankful for what we have.
